statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 5 (low) remains far below the block threshold: NQ trades 29,513.00, above Friday's 29,491.75 settlement, with the 29,274.75 overnight low intact for about seven hours and crude retreating from its highs. Stress 36 (moderate) reflects a $89.60 Brent risk premium, September rate-hike odds near 60% after the Jackson Hole remarks, and a month-end session that opens payrolls week.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers 13:30-14:30 UTC, where the U.S. cash open on the final August session meets month-end rebalancing, the Dallas Fed Manufacturing print and the first deep-liquidity pricing of the weekend Larak Island exchange. headline: Nasdaq-100: the overnight geopolitical shock stays fully retraced and the crude risk premium eases, leaving month-end rebalancing and near-60% September hike odds as the day's live checkpoints
body:
The recovery has held. The Nasdaq-100 September contract trades 29,513.00, up 21.25 points or 0.07% against Friday's 29,491.75 settlement, inside an overnight range of 29,274.75 to 29,545.50 on a quote timestamped 07:15 UTC. The 29,274.75 low was printed around the 00:00 UTC hour after the United States struck two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island and Iran's Revolutionary Guards answered with missiles at American bases in Jordan, eight of which Jordanian air defences intercepted without casualties. That low has now stood for roughly seven hours and the entire 236-point decline remains retraced. A completed retracement that then holds is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement path the tail measure is built to detect, so Tail eases a further point to 5, back to the level that prevailed through Friday's aftermath. S&P 500 futures at 7,709.75, down 0.16%, show the same broadly flat shape.

The second observable change this hour is in crude. Brent trades $89.60, up 1.70%, and WTI $84.66, up 1.52%, both below the $90.53 and $85.53 readings of an hour earlier. The Hormuz risk premium is therefore decaying rather than building, which is the cross-asset behaviour consistent with orderly absorption rather than escalation. Reporting continues to note that roughly six to eight million barrels a day still transit the strait and that traders frame the standoff in economic rather than imminent-supply terms.

The rates backdrop is unchanged and remains the larger Stress contributor. After Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks, fed funds futures price roughly a 60% chance of a quarter-point September increase, against odds of a hold near 70% before the speech. The Federal Reserve H.15 release shows the 2-year at 4.20% and the 10-year at 4.67%. VIX last printed 14.43 at Friday's cash close and is not a live input at this hour.

Today is the final August session. The Dow is up 2.1% for the month and on course for a fifth consecutive monthly advance, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite are up about 3% and 4% for their first monthly gains since May, led by semiconductors and AI-linked megacaps. That leaves month-end rebalancing as a mechanical flow concentrated into the 13:30 UTC open and the 20:00 UTC close, which is why the danger window is drawn narrowly around the open rather than across the session. The only scheduled U.S. release is the Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index at 14:30 UTC. The week's substance arrives later: ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS on Tuesday, ADP and the Beige Book on Wednesday, ISM Services on Thursday and August payrolls on Friday.

Stress falls to 36 as the crude premium eases while the rate-hike repricing and month-end mechanics persist. Confidence is 87, supported by a live NQ quote, S&P futures, both crude benchmarks, the H.15 curve, a verified calendar and verified reporting on the weekend escalation; the shared Finviz cross-asset context was more than five hours old at run time and was therefore treated as stale and excluded from the assessment.

lookbackSummary: Across the previous 24 hourly assessments Tail ran at 5 through Friday's aftermath and the quiet Sunday session, then stepped to 9 in the 22:00 UTC hour and peaked at 15 in the 00:00 UTC hour as the Larak Island exchange drove NQ to 29,274.75. Stress rose in parallel from 26 to a high of 44. Every hour since has walked Tail back - 13, 11, 10, 10, 8, 6 - as the overnight low held and the decline was fully retraced, and dominant mode moved from normal through trend-down to mixed. No hour reached the watch threshold and the mapped state stayed EA_ON throughout.
outlookSummary: The base case over the next 24 hours is continued two-way trade with Tail held in the 5 to 12 band and no hour reaching the 20 watch threshold, so the mapped state remains EA_ON across the window. Two narrow checkpoints carry the elevated conditional readings: the 13:30 UTC cash open on the final August session, where month-end rebalancing meets the Dallas Fed print and the first deep-liquidity pricing of the weekend escalation, and the 19:00 UTC hour into the 20:00 UTC close where that rebalancing settles. Stress peaks near 46 around the open and decays to the mid-30s overnight, while Confidence falls from 87 to 70 with distance from the 07:15 UTC live quote.
